stem: At one Massachusetts pharmacy a patient refuses to give any allergy history after being asked on three separate visits. At another, a patient is never asked because the queue is long. Both patient profiles are incomplete in exactly the same respect. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Both pharmacies are compliant, because the standard is only reasonable effort.
Both pharmacies are in breach, because the profile has to be complete.
Compliance turns on whether the missing history was clinically significant.
The first pharmacy made a reasonable effort and is compliant on these facts.
The second pharmacy made no effort at all and is not compliant.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.16(7) requires the pharmacist or the pharmacist's designee to make a REASONABLE EFFORT to obtain, record and maintain the listed information. The duty is measured by the effort made, not by the completeness of the resulting record, so identical gaps produce opposite results depending on what the pharmacy did.

choice_analysis.A: The second pharmacy made no effort, so the standard is not satisfied there.
choice_analysis.B: An incomplete profile is not automatically a breach.
choice_analysis.C: The standard is the effort made rather than the significance of the gap.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: repeated asking is a reasonable effort.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: a long queue does not excuse never asking.

related_facts: 247 CMR 9.16 does not apply to institutional sterile compounding pharmacies
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates grade the record rather than the effort, and so treat the two pharmacies alike.

reasoning_steps: Identify the standard as reasonable effort rather than completeness
Assess what each pharmacy actually did
Reach opposite conclusions on identical records
